2C.15 Blessings shall come to the man who fears the LORD.
2F.6 You shall walk in all the ways of the LORD your God.
13C.5 You shall eat the labor of your hands, and it shall be well with you.

precepts.text: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.
precepts.point: For thou shalt eat the labor of thine hands. There is profit in laboring, and this is not just the nine to five, it is laboring in this truth. We have too many people in IUIC who just talk and do not labor at all, and shame on you. You will escape this world by your works.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.” Walking in his ways is walking in God’s commandments: “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.” When we walk in the laws of the Lord we are undefiled; when we do not, we are defiled.

precepts.text: In all labor there is profit, but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.

precepts.text: Our sons as plants grown up in their youth, our daughters as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.
precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “thy children like olive plants round about thy table.” “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace”. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth: our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

precepts.text: Our garners full, affording all manner of store; our sheep bringing forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets.
precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets”. The wife is that fruitful vine by the sides of the house, the fruit of the womb that is his reward, a fruitful possession producing many children. The blessing fills everything: the garners full, the sheep bringing forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets.

precepts.text: Our oxen strong to labor, no breaking in nor going out; our businesses not taken and no going into slavery.
precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets.” Our oxen strong to labor, our businesses not taken, and no going out into slavery. That is the house where the wife is a fruitful vine and the children olive plants round about the table.

precepts.text: No complaining in our streets; happy is that people whose God is the Lord.
precepts.point: Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: No complaining in our streets: “Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the Lord.” The fruitful vine, the olive plants round about the table, the full garners and strong oxen all belong to that people whose God is the Lord.

precepts.text: The Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning with sheep, camels, oxen, and she asses.
precepts.point: Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “Yea, thou shalt see thy children’s children, and peace upon Israel.” There are plenty of benefits to keeping God’s laws and being blessed, and Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and “the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.”

precepts.text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
precepts.point: Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “He had also seven sons and three daughters.” After his trial Job was blessed in his latter end with children, the beginning of the children’s children he would live to see.

precepts.text: In all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; God blessed them.
precepts.point: Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.” God blessed them. Job’s daughters were the fairest in all the land and received inheritance among their brethren: the benefits of a man blessed in his latter end.

precepts.text: After this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and his sons' sons, even four generations.
precepts.point: Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.” This is “thou shalt see thy children’s children”. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters and blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

precepts.text: So Job died, being old and full of days.
precepts.point: Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why: “So Job died, being old and full of days.” That is the end of a man who kept God’s laws and was blessed: old and full of days, having seen his children’s children to four generations. Plenty of benefits come with keeping God’s laws, and peace upon Israel.
